- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) or flat, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 30d), model frequently overshoots; apply downward correction of 5–15% in next 5–7 days.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no sentiment signal, check for mean reversion; if price is above 30d moving average, reduce forecast slope.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and model forecast is rising, consider lag error — true price often lags model by 1–3 days; delay forecast peak by 1–2 days.
- If model forecast is flat or slightly declining while sentiment is positive, model may be missing momentum; increase forecast slope slightly.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from model, check sentiment history for 3–5 prior days — if any positive sentiment, model likely overcorrected.
